title: Cosmos · Carl Sagan · The fourth dimension
description: The complete supplied Flatland and fourth-dimension explanation, with physical narration and synchronized dimensional demonstrations.

characters.name: Carl Sagan
characters.role: The fourth dimension · CHIMERA physical voice

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: In discussing the large-scale structure of the cosmos,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: astronomers sometimes say that space is curved.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Or that the universe is finite but unbounded.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Whatever are they talking about?

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Let's imagine that we are perfectly flat. I mean absolutely flat.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: And that we live, appropriately enough,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: in a flat land.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: A land designed and named by Edwin Abbott,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: a Shakespearean scholar who lived in Victorian England.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Everybody in Flatland is, of course,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: exceptionally flat.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: We have squares,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: circles,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: triangles, and we all scurry about,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: and we can go into our houses and do our flat business.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now, we have width and length, but no height at all.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now, these little cutouts have some little height, but, uh...

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Let's ignore that. Let's imagine that these are absolutely flatlanders.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: That being the case,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: we know, us flatlanders, about left-right.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: We know about forward-back,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: but we have never heard of up-down.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Let us imagine that into flatland,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: hovering above it, comes a strange three-dimensional creature which,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: oddly enough, looks like an apple.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: And the three-dimensional creature sees an attractive,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: congenial-looking square,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: watches it enter its house,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: and decides, in a gesture of inter-dimensional amity,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: to say hello.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Hello, says the three-dimensional creature.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: How are you?

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: I am a visitor from the third dimension.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Well, the poor square looks around,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: his closed house,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: sees no one there,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: and what's more, has witnessed a greeting coming from his insides,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: a voice from within.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: He surely is getting a little worried about his sanity.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: The three-dimensional creature is unhappy about being considered a psychological aberration, And so he descends to actually enter Flatland.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now, a three-dimensional creature exists in Flatland only partially.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Only a plane, a cross-section through him,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: can be seen.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: So when the three-dimensional creature first reaches Flatland, it's only the points of contact which can be seen,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: and we'll represent that by stamping the apple in this ink pad,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: placing that image in Flatland.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: And as the apple were to descend through slither by flat land,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: we would progressively see higher and higher slices,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: which we can represent by

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: the apple.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: So the square,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: as time goes on,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: sees a set of objects mysteriously appear from nowhere and inside a closed room,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: and change their shape dramatically.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: His only conclusion could be that he's gone bonkers.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Well, the apple might be a little annoyed at this conclusion,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: and so,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: not such a friendly gesture from dimension to dimension,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: makes a contact with the square from below and sends our flat creature fluttering and spinning above flat land.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: At first, the square has no idea what's happening.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: It's terribly confused. This is utterly outside his experience.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: But after a while,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: he comes to realize that he is seeing inside closed rooms in Flatland.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: He is looking inside his fellow flat creatures.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: He is seeing Flatland from a perspective no one has ever seen it before to his knowledge.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Getting into another dimension provides as an incidental benefit a kind of x-ray vision.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now our flat creature slowly descends to the surface and his friends rush up to see him.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: From their point of view, he has mysteriously appeared from nowhere.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: He hasn't walked from somewhere else. He's come from some other place.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: They say, for heaven's sake, what's happened to you?

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: And the poor square has to say, well,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: I was in some other mystic dimension called Up.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: And they will pat him on his side and comfort him, or else they'll ask,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: well, show us, where is that third dimension?

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Point to it,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: and the poor square will be unable to comply.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: But maybe more interesting is the other direction in dimensionality.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: What about the fourth dimension?

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now, to approach that, let's consider a cube.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: We can imagine a cube in the following way.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: You take a line segment and move it at right angles to itself an equal length.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: That makes a square.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Move that square an equal length at right angles to itself,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: and you have a cube.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: this cube,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: we understand,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: casts a shadow.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: And

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: that shadow,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: we recognize.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: It's ordinarily drawn in third grade classrooms as two squares with their vertices connected.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now if we look at the shadow of a three-dimensional object in two dimensions, we see that in this case not all the lines appear equal.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Not all the angles are right angles.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: The three-dimensional object has not been perfectly represented in its projection in two dimensions,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: but that's part of the cost of losing a dimension in the projection.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: let's take this three-dimensional cube and project it, carry it through a fourth physical dimension.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Not that way,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: not that way,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: not that way,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: but at right angles to those three directions.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: I can't show you what direction that is, but imagine that there is a fourth physical dimension.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: In that case, we would generate a four-dimensional hypercube,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: which is also called a tesseract.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: I cannot show you a tesseract, because I and you are trapped in three dimensions.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: But what I can show you is the shadow in three dimensions of a four-dimensional hypercube or tesseract.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: This is it.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: And you can see it's two nested cubes,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: all the vertices connected by lines.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: And now the real tesseract in four dimensions would have all the lines of equal length and all the angles right angles.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: That's not what we see here, but that's the penalty of projection.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: So,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: you see, while we cannot imagine the world of four dimensions,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: we can certainly think about it perfectly well.

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: Now,

cues.speaker: sagan
cues.text: imagine a universe just like Flatland truly
